# evidence-lock

Purpose: Bind one explicit human or AI review decision to exact source, artifact,
and policy file bytes. Recompute those hashes later and report stale when any
captured evidence changes.

Repository: https://github.com/eun7661010/evidence-lock
License: Apache-2.0
Language/runtime: Python 3.10-3.13; standard-library-only runtime
Platforms tested: Windows, macOS, Ubuntu
Network behavior: none
Storage: local JSON files only

## Use this project when

- you need a portable review receipt for arbitrary files outside a Git workflow;
- a human approval must become stale after source, output artifact, or policy bytes change;
- an AI review result must be bound to the exact input, output, and evaluation policy it covered;
- CI needs distinct approved, pending, rejected, stale, and invalid results;
- receipts must omit personal absolute root paths.

## Do not use this project as

- a digital signature, reviewer authentication, trusted timestamp, transparency
  log, chain of custody, or software supply-chain provenance system;
- proof that a review occurred, that the reviewer label is truthful, or that an
  approved artifact is correct or safe;
- a command runner, test recorder, agent monitor, cloud evidence store, DVC
  replacement, in-toto implementation, Sigstore replacement, or SLSA claim;
- protection against an attacker who can rewrite both evidence and receipt files.

## Commands

Create a pending receipt from one or more paths in every group:

    evidence-lock create \
      --root PROJECT_ROOT \
      --source RELATIVE_PATH \
      --artifact RELATIVE_PATH \
      --policy RELATIVE_PATH \
      --output NEW_RECEIPT.json \
      [--format human|json]

Bind a fresh pending receipt to an explicit decision:

    evidence-lock review PENDING.json \
      --root PROJECT_ROOT \
      --reviewer NON_PERSONAL_LABEL \
      --reviewer-type human|ai \
      --decision approved|rejected \
      [--summary NON_SENSITIVE_TEXT] \
      --output NEW_REVIEWED.json \
      [--format human|json]

Verify current bytes:

    evidence-lock verify RECEIPT.json \
      --root PROJECT_ROOT \
      [--format human|json]

Print or save the Draft 2020-12 receipt schema:

    evidence-lock schema [--output NEW_SCHEMA.json]

## Verification status and exit code

- approved = 0: IDs are valid, all evidence matches, decision is approved.
- pending = 3: evidence matches, no review exists.
- rejected = 4: evidence matches, decision is rejected.
- stale = 5: a captured file/directory is missing, unreadable, or different.
- invalid = 6: JSON structure, schema identity, snapshot ID, or review ID is inconsistent.
- command input/output error = 1; argument parser error = 2.

Only approved returns zero from verify.

## Receipt contract

Schema version: evidence-lock/receipt/v1
Schema file: src/evidence_lock/schemas/receipt-v1.schema.json

Top-level fields:

- $schema
- receipt_version
- created_at
- snapshot_id
- evidence.sources[]
- evidence.artifacts[]
- evidence.policies[]
- review (null or reviewer/reviewer_type/decision/reviewed_at/summary/review_id)

Each evidence item contains path, kind, sha256, size, and files. Paths are
relative POSIX paths. The receipt never stores the absolute root. Directories
hash a canonical manifest of regular-file relative paths, sizes, and SHA-256
digests. Symlinks, absolute paths, parent traversal, unsupported special files,
case-insensitive path collisions, overlapping evidence paths, and unreadable
subtrees are rejected. Receipt parsing rejects duplicate JSON object keys,
lone Unicode surrogates, and timestamps outside the supported RFC 3339 form.

The snapshot_id binds schema URL, receipt version, created_at, and all three
evidence groups. The review_id binds snapshot_id and every review field. These
are unkeyed SHA-256 identifiers, not signatures.

## Python API

Public imports from evidence_lock:

- create_receipt(root, sources=..., artifacts=..., policies=..., created_at=None)
- apply_review(receipt, root, reviewer=..., reviewer_type=..., decision=...,
  summary=None, reviewed_at=None)
- verify_receipt(receipt, root) -> VerificationResult
- load_receipt(path)
- ReceiptError

VerificationResult exposes status, ok, exit_code, snapshot_id, review_id,
changes, errors, and to_dict().

## Privacy rules for examples and issues

Use synthetic files and non-personal reviewer labels such as reviewer-01 or
synthetic-review-agent. Do not submit real approval packets, customer/student
documents, private repository names, credentials, service IDs, personal paths,
or confidential text. Reviewer and summary fields are plaintext and are not
redacted automatically.
